items.title: SME S109 — Replace request polling with a streaming duplex session
items.scope: Live-path transport only; ledger, storage and Atlas boundaries unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Browser and service exchange audio and turn events over one authenticated local streaming session; no polling loop remains on the live path.
Every event carries session, turn, transcript revision and generation identifiers so a late result can neither speak nor mutate the current turn.
Disconnect and restart resume the session with an explicit audio-gap notice.
Push-to-talk continues to work when streaming is unavailable, as a fallback rather than the default path.

items.title: SME S110 — Listen continuously with voice-activity detection and streaming recognition
items.scope: Capture, voice-activity detection, endpointing and recogniser selection; extends the recognition evidence in #1520.
acceptance_criteria: The microphone stays open for the agreed session with a visible state and a working mute; partial transcripts stabilise while the participant speaks.
A persistent streaming recogniser replaces per-utterance process spawning; base.en is compared with at least one larger local model on numbers, negation, acronyms, hesitation and noise.
Premature turn-cut rate at or below 5 per cent on labelled turn cases, reported with numerator and denominator; hesitation and silence are distinguished from a completed thought.
Provisional text remains provisional: only stabilised or confirmed wording can support a claim.

items.title: SME S111 — Stop speaking when the participant speaks
items.scope: Acoustic barge-in and echo handling on the confirmed headset.
acceptance_criteria: Confirmed participant speech onset to cessation of played output at or below 250 ms p95 on labelled cases.
Echo cancellation prevents the interviewer's own output being treated as participant speech; evidence covers headset playback.
Queued and in-flight synthesis and generation are cancelled; no stale response speaks after an interruption.
A participant pause, mute or button press always takes precedence over any model plan.

items.title: SME S112 — Split the fast talker from the background thinker
items.scope: Question planning and response composition; check placement follows ADR-013 and ADR-014.
acceptance_criteria: Coverage assessment, claim drafting, evidence matching and agenda maintenance run from partial transcripts while the participant is still speaking.
The spoken reply is produced by a fast non-reasoning local model from the prepared agenda; no model review call remains on the critical path.
End of speech to first substantive audio at p50 at or below 1.5 s and p95 at or below 3 s over at least 100 in-browser turns, instrumented per SME-S114.
Pre-rendered filler that only masks delay is removed; any acknowledgement is contextual and is reported separately from the substantive response.
Ledger, draft and publication checks are unchanged and keep their full model review off the speech path.

items.title: SME S113 — Speak in streamed clauses with an acknowledgement bank
items.scope: Synthesis boundary and playback only; voice selection stays with SME-S118.
acceptance_criteria: Synthesis emits first audio within 400 ms of the first checked clause instead of waiting for a complete file.
Cancellation works at clause granularity and leaves no orphaned audio.
Short acknowledgements are pre-rendered and served without a model request; they never carry facts, numbers or names.
Synthesis may alter prosody, never content; number, date and negation rendering regressions remain green.

items.title: SME S114 — Instrument the real turn gap in the browser
items.scope: Measurement and reporting only.
acceptance_criteria: Each turn records endpoint decision, final transcript, first generated token, first audio and playback start with browser-side timestamps.
Per-session latency distributions are exportable and are reported with every conversational iteration, cold start separately from warm.
Reported figures state their sample size; stage figures are never summed into an end-to-end claim.

items.title: SME S115 — Let the interviewer speak like an interviewer
items.scope: Response grammar, persona and speech-safety checks; replaces the bare-question validator.
acceptance_criteria: A turn may contain a brief acknowledgement or reflection, an optional bridge or cited evidence, and one question; the single question-only validator is replaced by the ADR-013 speech-safety check.
Speech safety rejects any number, name, date or factual assertion not present in the participant's own words or a cited eligible excerpt.
The session has an opening that introduces the assistant and purpose, a stated recording and correction position, a time check and a closing.
Humour stays optional and light, is never aimed at a person's competence, accent or memory, and is absent when presenting a disagreement.
The example exchanges published in the interview-experience page can be reproduced by the running service.

items.title: SME S116 — Listen actively and confirm at the recap
items.scope: Backchannels, reflection and the confirmation model per ADR-016.
acceptance_criteria: Sparse optional backchannels signal attention and are never recorded as agreement.
The interviewer reflects the account back periodically in speech, and asks a spoken check only for high-impact ambiguity such as numbers, names and negation.
Per-turn transcript confirmation is removed from the voice path; contribution kind is inferred and corrected by the participant at the recap.
Every claim in the draft still traces to recap-confirmed wording and its transcript revision; unconfirmed material cannot enter a packet.
A correction at recap invalidates dependent derived notes exactly as a per-turn correction does today.

items.title: SME S117 — Interrupt respectfully and only when it earns it
items.scope: Interruption policy and participant controls; uses live evidence from SME-S121 when available.
acceptance_criteria: An unsolicited interruption requires a stable transcript, an identifiable question, and either a cited same-scope comparator or a critical capture problem.
A configurable cooldown and a single pending interruption prevent repeated challenge on one point; gentle, balanced and on-request settings are selectable during a session.
Non-urgent discrepancies are queued during a free account rather than interrupting it.
Interruption appropriateness is rated in trials and reported in aggregate, never as a judgement of the participant.

items.title: SME S118 — Choose the voice on conversational speech, not read passages
items.scope: Blinded conversational listening comparison with streamed first-chunk timing.
acceptance_criteria: Samples cover acknowledgement, reflection, a kind challenge and light humour, not only read passages.
At least one expressive British English challenger is compared with Voice B using streamed first-chunk timing rather than complete-file timing.
Content fidelity for numbers, dates and negation remains a mandatory gate regardless of the preference score.
The selection records sample size and individual variation and does not generalise from one listener.

items.title: SME S119 — Measure conversation quality against simulated participants
items.scope: Repeatable local harness and a Human rating sheet; repository automation only.
acceptance_criteria: Simulated participants hold a hidden ground-truth process with planted contradictions, unknowns, corrections and a genuine same-scope conflict.
A published rubric scores relevance, repetition, premise errors, listening behaviour and pace; development and holdout personas stay separate and the holdout is not tuned against.
Every iteration reports rubric scores and the SME-S114 turn-gap distribution alongside structural test results.
A one-page Human rating sheet captures naturalness, comfort, usefulness and fatigue.
No ADO Test Plans, Test Suites or Test Cases are created.

items.title: SME S120 — Derive the interview agenda from the Atlas ontology
items.scope: Read-only Atlas adapter and agenda construction; completes the evidence-pack intent of #1523.
acceptance_criteria: The agenda is built for a selected process from the Atlas ontology, Process Registry and Enterprise Activity Model: what is already held and can be verified, what is absent and must be elicited, and where existing sources disagree.
A second, materially different synthetic process runs end to end with no code change; fixture-specific wording and regular-expression guards are removed from the planner.
Evidence is pinned at session start with source version and hash; a changed or revoked pack blocks comparison rather than silently continuing.
Standalone operation without Atlas still works and states plainly that no evidence is available.
The adapter remains read-only: no Atlas source, section store or ontology write occurs.

items.title: SME S121 — Challenge and give back inside the live budget
items.scope: Live evidence lane within the 350 ms budget; no automatic conflict determination.
acceptance_criteria: The session evidence pack is prefetched and embedded at session start so a live comparison meets the 350 ms live-lane budget; budget expiry yields unchecked or needs-review, never verified.
Any spoken evidence statement quotes an eligible excerpt verbatim with its scope and version, and distinguishes what a source says from what is correct.
Live challenge precision at or above 95 per cent on labelled cases, with recall reported separately; a missing retrieval hit is never presented as absence of knowledge.
The interviewer can offer a relevant fact when asked or when it benefits the participant, always cited, and never fills a knowledge gap from model memory.
Deferred and background adjudication continue to own everything the live lane cannot settle.

items.title: SME S122 — Keep the session inside its time box
items.scope: Pacing, parking and hand-off to deferred validation.
acceptance_criteria: The agenda is paced against the agreed session length with a spoken time check; topics can be parked and the session extended only by agreement.
At the limit the session closes with uncovered topics listed explicitly rather than silently truncated.
Parked and unresolved points hand off to the deferred validation and follow-up work in #1532 and #1537.

items.title: SME S123 — Record the G1.5 conversation gate decision
items.scope: Human acceptance decision; no implementation work.
acceptance_criteria: A ten-minute unscripted headset conversation on a synthetic process runs with no button press between turns and no per-turn confirmation.
Human median rating at or above 4 of 5 for naturalness and pace, measured p50 at or below 1.5 s from end of speech to first substantive audio, and zero fabricated spoken facts.
The outcome, date and rationale are recorded in this Story and in the repository decision register.
A failed gate returns specific findings to SME-F13, SME-F14 or SME-F15; acceptance criteria are never lowered to pass it.

items.title: SME F17 — Tiberius sales workspace and product recall
items.gate: Internal sales rehearsal review; not customer or G1.5 acceptance
items.scope: User-authorised iterations 1 and 2 on 24 September: separate clean OpsAtlas Sales data and Tiberius product recall. Preserve existing corpus. Local-only voice; no wake-name or customer meeting delivery.
acceptance_criteria: Separate data, sessions, credentials and UI; existing workspace is not mutated.
Product records retain provenance and explicit internal review.
Spoken recall cites eligible evidence or reports unavailable knowledge.
User acceptance remains open; no automatic customer-claim approval.

items.title: SME S124 — Isolate OpsAtlas Sales without changing existing knowledge
items.gate: Internal sales rehearsal review; not customer or G1.5 acceptance
items.scope: Separate Atlas core and built Control Panel on 8780; Tiberius on 8773 with isolated ledger. Explicit marker, storage guard, local credential, startup script and regression evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Ignore inherited original KP_DATA_DIR; reject unmarked stores and unsafe links.
Registration, ingestion, native approval/rejection and rebuild stay inside the sales workspace.
Launch checks identity; Control Panel uses the sales API origin and labels the workspace.
Original-data sentinel remains unchanged in integration tests.

items.title: SME S125 — Recall reviewed OpsAtlas product knowledge through Tiberius
items.gate: Internal sales rehearsal review; not customer or G1.5 acceptance
items.scope: Eight pending curated records plus copied hashed originals. Local model chooses source IDs; exact eligible text is spoken via Chatterbox with visible evidence. Human enables records for internal rehearsal only.
acceptance_criteria: Distinguish available, experimental and unknown product claims; no invented pricing or ROI.
Unapproved, rejected, deleted or hash-changed evidence cannot answer a new question.
Revalidate selected evidence after inference and display citation information.
Demonstrate overview, offline/avatar distinction, pricing unknown and unsupported guarantee with real local speech.
Owner reviews the delivered corpus and accepts recall behaviour before story closure.

items.title: SME S126 — Interview contributors and review product knowledge additions
items.gate: Internal product interview acceptance; not customer publication or full E2 completion
items.scope: Local product interview with Chris/Dan attribution, provisional source-linked wording, review/correction and explicit relationship decisions before internal recall. Preserve original Atlas data.
acceptance_criteria: Product mode persists contributor/topic across saved sessions; source attribution is server-bound.
Cancelled stale responses cannot create proposals; model output cannot approve claims.
Exact retries reuse sources; corrections withdraw old approval and bind new review to provenance.
Uncertain/disputed claims cannot answer; scoped resolution or supersession is explicitly reviewed.
Approved additions are recalled with current source hashes; demonstrate browser review and real local recall in a disposable workspace.
Owner checks headset conversation quality and claim review before closure.

items.title: SME F18 — Tiberius speed, grounding and retrieval remediation (independent review 2)
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Independent review 2 (24 September 2026) of the Tiberius sales companion and the conversational core. Measured end of speech to first audio: median 4.6 s over 49 live microphone turns, about 9 s with the Higgs voice, against the G1.5 target of 1.5 s. The live layered companion can speak unchecked product claims, and Tiberius bypasses the OpsAtlas retriever.   Human decision 24 September: Claude owns delivery of every item except the licence decision (S148, deferred while in evaluation). Higgs stays the live voice and is to be made fast.   Repository: docs/initiatives/sme-interviewer/41-independent-review-2.md
acceptance_criteria: Replay harness median end of speech to first audio at or below 1.5 s, reported per stage with p50 and p95 over at least 100 turns.
No product claim is spoken unless it has been checked against enabled, hash-valid records before speech.
Product evidence is retrieved through the OpsAtlas hybrid retriever over enabled records only.
Branch green in the ADO pipeline on Python 3.11 through a pull request; the Human evaluates before merge.

items.title: SME S127 — Stream the Tibi turn end to end
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Model tokens become speakable clauses, then Higgs audio chunks, then playback, with cancellation on barge-in. Replaces wait-for-complete at every stage.
acceptance_criteria: The first clause is sent to speech before the model has finished the reply.
Barge-in cancels generation, synthesis and playback of the stale turn.
Timing marks include first token, first clause and first audio.

items.title: SME S128 — Stream Higgs audio in chunks with a reused voice prompt
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Higgs currently renders a whole reply or its first sentence group before releasing audio (3–12.5 s).
acceptance_criteria: Higgs first audio chunk measured for short and long replies, reported separately from reasoning.
The voice identity, reference and accepted settings are unchanged.
No audible seams between chunks in the automated waveform checks.

items.title: SME S129 — Pre-render approved product answers in the Higgs voice
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Approved record text, and spoken variants a human has approved, are synthesised ahead of time so product answers start immediately.
acceptance_criteria: Only approved wording is pre-rendered; model drafts stay pending until a human approves them.
A record hash change invalidates its audio and spoken variants.
A pre-rendered product answer starts in under 150 ms after routing.

items.title: SME S130 — Close a confident turn after 0.3–0.4 s of silence
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Endpointing currently enforces a 1.0 s silence floor regardless of the turn model's confidence.
acceptance_criteria: High-confidence turn completion closes after the short floor; uncertain turns keep the long wait.
Resumed speech still cancels the endpoint.
Endpoint p50 below 0.5 s in the replay harness.

items.title: SME S131 — Prepare Tibi's reply from the settled partial transcript
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: The companion path starts only after the final transcript. The interview path already speculates; Tibi does not.
acceptance_criteria: Reply preparation starts from a settled partial and is reused only when the final transcript matches.
Nothing is spoken, committed or saved before the endpoint.
Mismatched speculation is cancelled.

items.title: SME S132 — Route first, then stream the spoken reply as plain text
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: About 30 of 55–95 generated tokens are JSON scaffolding emitted before the reply.
acceptance_criteria: The routing decision is made before generation.
The reply streams as text.
Invalid or unsafe streamed text aborts before it is spoken.

items.title: SME S133 — Keep Tibi's models resident for the session and warm before listening
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: A 5-minute keep_alive unloads the model, and the cold load costs 2.8 s.
acceptance_criteria: Models stay loaded while a session is open.
Warm-up completes before the microphone opens.
No cold load on the first turn.

items.title: SME S134 — Keep the background evidence check away from the foreground turn
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: The post-speech check competes with the next turn and is silently lost on interruption.
acceptance_criteria: The check yields while the user is speaking and resumes afterwards.
An unfinished check is recorded as unavailable, never dropped.
Foreground latency is unaffected in the harness.

items.title: SME S135 — Send every product-related or uncertain turn through the evidence layer
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Today a reply labelled conversation or general is spoken unchecked unless it contains the literal word OpsAtlas.
acceptance_criteria: Cost, pricing, ROI, security, certification, capability, deployment and customer claims are routed to evidence whether or not the product is named.
Uncertain routing defaults to evidence.
Regression probes from the review cannot produce an unchecked product claim.

items.title: SME S136 — Verify spoken product wording against the cited records before speech
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Only record IDs and hashes are checked today, not the wording.
acceptance_criteria: Numbers, prices, percentages, standards, capability terms and negations in the spoken answer must be supported by the cited records.
An unsupported answer falls back to approved wording or a specific not-established reply.
The insufficient status can no longer carry an invented fact.

items.title: SME S137 — Check product answers before they are spoken; never lose a check silently
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: The evidence review currently runs after audio and is cancelled without trace on interruption.
acceptance_criteria: No generated product wording reaches speech before verification.
Interrupted checks are recorded.
Conflicts found later are raised to the user in the next turn.

items.title: SME S138 — Restrict the product interviewer to enabled records
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Pending, rejected and disputed records are passed to the model and can be spoken.
acceptance_criteria: Only enabled, hash-valid records are shown to the interviewer model.
A test proves a disputed claim cannot be read back.

items.title: SME S139 — Keep planned and not-yet-verified qualifiers in spoken answers
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Paraphrase can drop the qualifier the record carries.
acceptance_criteria: An answer citing a planned or unverified record states that qualification in speech.
Tests cover paraphrased answers.

items.title: SME S140 — Retrieve product evidence through the OpsAtlas hybrid retriever
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Tiberius passes the first 24 enabled records to the prompt and silently drops the rest.
acceptance_criteria: Enabled records are ranked by the platform retriever (BM25 plus embeddings) with a relevance threshold.
Degrades to lexical-only when embeddings are unavailable.
No silent truncation.

items.title: SME S141 — Replace keyword routing with similarity to the records
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Phrase lists and hard-coded record IDs are tuned to specific test sentences.
acceptance_criteria: Routing uses record similarity plus a small product-claim lexicon, not transcript-specific phrases.
The hard-coded overview and process IDs and the forced how-it-works mapping are removed.

items.title: SME S142 — Cache the enabled catalogue by content hash
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: The catalogue is fetched twice per product turn.
acceptance_criteria: A single cached catalogue per turn, keyed by content hash.
Revalidated before speech.

items.title: SME S143 — Collapse the companion stack into one explicit Tibi turn pipeline
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Companion, SalesCompanion and LayeredCompanion are stacked; the tested exact-excerpt path is not the live path.
acceptance_criteria: One pipeline module is used by the live service.
Dead paths are removed.
Tests exercise the live path.

items.title: SME S144 — Restore the core Avatar prompt and keep Tibi delivery rules in the voice service
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Tibi delivery rules were injected into the core Avatar natural-style prompt without an Avatar evaluation.
acceptance_criteria: Core Avatar prompt restored to its prior wording.
Tibi rules live in the voice service.
Core tests pass.

items.title: SME S145 — Make the branch CI-green on Python 3.11 and deliver through a pull request
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: 25 commits never ran through the pipeline; one test fails on 3.11 because asyncio.wait_for swallowed an interruption's cancellation.
acceptance_criteria: Full suite green on Python 3.11.
PR to main raised and the ADO build green.
No merge without the Human's evaluation.

items.title: SME S146 — Separate experiments from the live Tiberius service
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Voice-rating pages mounted on the sales service write into a runtime shared with the non-sales service.
acceptance_criteria: The live sales service no longer mounts experiment pages.
Experiments run from their own entry point.
A cleanup list of unused trial models is supplied to the Human.

items.title: SME S147 — Automated replay latency harness
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: The largest measured sample is 5 turns, against the gate's 100.
acceptance_criteria: Replays synthetic spoken questions through the live turn path in a disposable workspace.
At least 100 turns with per-stage p50 and p95.
Results saved as evidence.

items.title: SME S148 — Decide commercial licence and speaker consent for the Higgs voice
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Deferred by the Human on 24 September 2026 while Tiberius remains in evaluation. The downloaded Higgs, Fish and Breeze licences permit evaluation only; the live reference is a VCTK speaker.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded before any use beyond private evaluation.

items.title: SME S149 — Reconcile ADO, README and backlog manifest with delivered work
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: The 21 September work has no ADO record; the README and backlog.json are stale; the sales-companion direction is recorded only in Codex's words.
acceptance_criteria: ADO, README, backlog.json and ado-links.json agree.
A handover log entry is recorded.

items.title: SME S150 — Corrections from the Human's first Tiberius headset evaluation
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Two headset sessions on 25 September 2026 (29 turns; end of speech to playback median about 2.1 s). The Human liked the speed, asked that it must not creep back, and asked that questions about Tibi are answered personally ("It is me!") with light humour.
acceptance_criteria: Statements, social requests and conversation requests are not answered from product records.
Questions about Tibi are answered in the first person, warmly, grounded and still experimental.
Background sound captions are ignored.
Background checks raise only anchored conflicts.
A latency budget fails the replay if speed regresses; headset latency is reportable per session.

items.title: SME S151 — Foundation product knowledge from the DT603 Part A paper
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: The Human chose their DT603 Part A paper as the canonical account of what OpsAtlas is (25 September 2026), to be refined later through the interview workflow. Decisions: a fresh sales workspace (the previous one archived, not deleted); commercial projections left out; no build-story record.
acceptance_criteria: A local product edition of the paper is extracted and never committed; excluded parts are documented.
Curated records drawn from the paper cite their sections and pages, pass the claim checker and stay pending until the Human enables them.
Interview topics follow the records in use.
The previous workspace is archived and a fresh one seeded.

items.title: SME S152 — Corrections from the Human's second Tiberius evaluation
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: Headset session on 25 September 2026 (16 turns; latest session median end of speech to playback 1.38 s). Feedback: a broad security question went straight into data anonymisation instead of asking which area; asked about real use, Tibi said the data would stay anonymised, which is only true of the proof-of-concept demo; "How accurate is it?" twice produced "could you say that again" because a long approved answer exceeded the voice worker's 600-character request limit.
acceptance_criteria: Approved wording longer than one voice request is split into sentence groups; no answer fails for its length.
A broad topic question (security) is answered with the areas Tibi can cover and a question; the chosen area is answered from its records, and the topic is not narrowed twice.
Answers about real use distinguish the proof-of-concept demo from a real deployment, from a planned record the Human enables.
Qualifiers follow the sentence they qualify; a percentage in digits or words is the same figure.
The replay stays within the latency budget.

items.title: SME S153 — OpsAtlas product ontology for Tibi and the sales pitch
items.gate: Independent review 2 remediation; Human evaluation before merge
items.scope: The Human chose option 2 on 25 September 2026: Tibi should use an ontology layer, which should also help the sales pitch. A curated product ontology (capabilities, components, limitations, broad topics and their aspects) is built in the platform OntologyStore with its own schema and database, from enabled records only. The core ontology is not touched.
acceptance_criteria: Every ontology object names the curated records that establish it and exists only while all of them are enabled.

Named product parts (the ontology layer, the Enterprise Activity Model) route to product evidence; ontology facts and their records join the evidence pack and pass the claim checker against the records.
Whole-product questions (delivered versus planned, where it runs, limitations, components) are answered from ontology facts.
The ontology is visible read-only in Knowledge review, including objects waiting on records.

items.title: SME F19 — Governance interviews with Tibi
items.scope: The Human asked on 25 September 2026 to resolve the compliance, consistency and correctness issues in OpsAtlas Governance through the interview flow rather than by editing the solution. Tibi takes the open issues in priority order, explains each one with the passages involved, verifies the answer against the sources immediately, and saves it for the Human to approve in the system.
acceptance_criteria: Open Quick Scan issues are presented in priority order, with the passages involved and what the corpus already says.
Every answer is verified against the sources before it is read back; conflicts and unsupported statements are named.
Nothing is saved until the Human confirms, and nothing is resolved until the Human approves; sources are never edited.
Approval closes the issue in OpsAtlas Governance through the platform action, with the answer as its record.

items.title: SME S154 — Conversation and sales intent from the Human's third evaluation
items.scope: Headset session on 25 September 2026 (15 turns; median end of speech to playback 1.41 s). The small talk the Human liked had gone; politics was answered from stale model knowledge; prospect and repair questions were mishandled; answers lacked the sales intent, which should be captured through interviews rather than hard-coded.
acceptance_criteria: Small talk is conversation, playful and honest; the chat may drift to everyday topics.
Politics, current officeholders, religion and crude requests get a light decline; profanity is never spoken.
A complaint that a question was not answered re-answers the earlier question from evidence.
Conversation style is governed OpsAtlas data the Human enables, never product evidence.
Product answers relate to the prospect's organisation where the records support it; the proof-of-concept-to-production story is captured by interview.
The replay stays within the latency budget.

items.title: SME S155 — Tibi interviews the Human about open governance issues
items.scope: A governance interview mode for Tibi over the isolated sales workspace: agenda from the platform Quick Scan (acronyms grouped across sources, standard abbreviations batched), explanations from the exact passages and corpus definitions, instant verification against the sources, pending answers, and approval in Knowledge review that closes issues through the platform accept_issue action.
acceptance_criteria: The agenda lists open issues in priority order and one question per acronym, with the passages involved.
Answers are verified against source definitions, mentions and claim vocabulary before read-back.
An answer is saved as pending only after the Human confirms it; a turn has no side effects until committed.
Approval closes each settled issue in OpsAtlas Governance; an acronym issue closes when all its acronyms are answered.
Commands: skip, repeat, go back, how many are left, stop.

items.title: SME S156 — Governance interview navigation and overlap passages from the Human's fourth evaluation
items.scope: Headset session on 25 September 2026 (30 turns; median end of speech to playback 1.42 s). The conversation went well; the governance interview was easy to confuse: requests to hear the other passage, go to a question or wait were recorded as resolutions; unclear replies in the confirm step re-asked the issue question; duplicates read only the first passage.
acceptance_criteria: Navigation (go to question N, back, skip, start again, check again, how many left, hold on) and requests for information are handled before anything is treated as an answer, and are never saved.
Duplicates are explained with the overlapping sentences from both documents, read aloud and shown on the page.
In the confirm step, yes (including "awesome"), no and "not yet" are understood; anything unclear re-asks the confirm question, and the saved answer is the substantive one.
Unclear answers are met with the choices for that issue.
Meta-talk is not verified as a claim; Tibi adopts a corrected word; guidance examples are not echoed.
The replay stays within the latency budget.

items.title: SME S157 — Tibi inside the OpsAtlas control panel
items.scope: The Human decided on 25 September 2026 that Tibi's experience and review workflow belong in OpsAtlas itself, not on separate pages: Talk with Tibi and Tibi knowledge become control-panel pages, governance interview answers are approved on the Governance page, and the separate pages retire.
acceptance_criteria: A Tibi group in the OpsAtlas sidebar (shown only when the workspace runs Tibi) with Talk with Tibi and Tibi knowledge.
Tibi knowledge offers everything the separate review page did: records, conversation style, spoken answers, interview contributions and the product ontology.
The Governance page shows the governance interview answers for approval beside the issues, and Resolve with Tibi opens a governance interview.
Every Tibi action in the control panel requires the OpsAtlas operator sign-in; proposal attribution still comes from the saved interview.
The voice service serves only the conversation embedded in OpsAtlas; its former pages redirect to the OpsAtlas pages.
